findings.title: All success criteria traced; sequencing and commit points sound
findings.description: Mapping (criterion → task): PASS/exit-0 for designs that pass the script → Task 4 + Task 4T "Real slice designs" + Task 5 step 6 parity sweep; `FAIL`/`  missing: <heading>`/exit 1 → Task 2 (original text preserved), Task 4 human output, Task 2T ordering assertion; doctype message → Task 3 per-file branch + Task 3T + Task 4T; in-order multi-file with later files still checked → Task 3 ("A failing file does not stop later files") + Task 3T/4T; the whole exit-2 set including the valid-file-before-missing case and the `cf guides update` message → Task 3 preflight + Task 4 `handleError(err, 2)` with nothing on stdout + Task 3T/4T; `--json` contract → Task 4 + Task 4T; worktree-owned template → Task 4 (`resolveProjectWorktree`/`resolveOperationPath`) + Task 4T reusing `validate-worktree-scope.test.ts`; the normalization/matching unit-test list (case, whitespace, comments, parentheticals, placeholder prefix, level mismatch, fenced block, CRLF) → Task 2T item by item; the real-template file-level test asserting `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough` → Task 3T (I confirmed both are marked-required headings in `templates/slice-design.md:33` and `:140`); build/lint/full suite and ~300-line limits → Task 6 plus per-task Success lines; Verification Walkthrough steps 1–6 → Task 5. Dependencies flow one way (0→1→2→2T→3→3T→4→4T→5→6) and Task 1 correctly has no commit marker (it is a single constant with no test of its own, landing in 2C). I/O semantics for exit 2 check out: `handleError` writes to stderr and calls `process.exit` in both modes, so stdout stays empty as the design requires.

findings.title: Task 4T's `--json` exit-2 assertions need the JSON-mode flag set explicitly in-process
findings.description: Task 4T requires "Exit 2 with empty stdout, in human and `--json` mode" and says to follow the setup in `validate.test.ts`. `validate.test.ts` exercises JSON output through `printJson`, which keys off `opts.json` from the parsed command line — that works with `program.parseAsync`. But `handleError`'s error path keys off `isJsonMode()`, and JSON mode is only set at CLI entry load (`setJsonMode()` when `process.argv.includes('--json')`) or via `CF_JSON`. In a vitest in-process harness neither happens. The named criterion ("nothing on stdout") still passes either way, so this is not a gap — but the `--json` half of the test would silently assert the human-mode stderr shape. Cheap fix in the task file: state that the test sets `process.env.CF_JSON = '1'` (or calls `setJsonMode()`) in the `--json` cases. The same task-file note also deserves one line about mocking `process.exit`, since `handleError` calls it; `validate.test.ts` does so only in its single exit-2 test, while the exit-2 list in Task 4T has four cases — `validate-worktree-scope.test.ts` already shows the pattern needed and Task 4T cites it only for the worktree fixture.

findings.title: The 214 design doc is both a test fixture and a file Task 5 edits
findings.description: Task 3T pins "Real design: `project-documents/user/slices/214-...md` passes against the real template," and Task 5's fourth step tells the implementer to write a "Parity differences" list into that same document's Implementation Notes. The edit adds a heading under `## Implementation Notes`, which cannot remove a required heading, so the test should still pass — but the ordering makes a previously-green file-level test depend on a later doc edit, and a careless insertion (e.g. nesting a `###` where a required `##` was deleted) would surface as a failure in an unrelated task. Consider either running the suite again after the Task 5 edit (Task 6's full `pnpm test` does this, so the risk is covered) or having Task 5 add the notes under a subheading only, explicitly. No action strictly required.

findings.title: "Wrap any unexpected `fs` error" cannot cover `parseFrontmatter`'s internal swallow
findings.description: Task 3 says to wrap unexpected `fs` errors in `SliceDesignValidationError` so every I/O failure exits 2. `parseFrontmatter` never throws — it returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` from a `catch` around its own `readFile`. The preflight step already satisfies the "unreadable file → exit 2" criterion (regular-file + readable check before any validation), so this only matters in a TOCTOU race, where the file would be reported as `reason: 'doctype'` (FAIL, exit 1) instead of exit 2. Worth one line in Task 3 so the implementer doesn't expect the wrapper to catch it, or an explicit comment in the code noting preflight owns that guarantee. Flagging for awareness only — no requirement is left unmet.

findings.title: Commit markers are their own checklist items rather than plain lines
findings.description: `Task 2C/3C/4C: Commit` are written as `- [ ] **Task ...: Commit** — \`<message>\`` checkboxes, not the `**Commit**:` plain-line form. They sit at correct working, tested points (after each implementation+test pair, conditional for Tasks 5 and 6), which is the substantive requirement, and the checkbox form matches accepted precedent in this repo's own task files (`161`, `162`, `169`, `170`), where AGENTS.md's blanket checklist rule applies. The `5C`/`6C` "only if Task N changed files" conditions are a good touch — they prevent empty commits. Noted only so the format choice is deliberate.
